What this is

Managed Detection & Response

Managed Detection & Response (MDR) is a 24/7 operated service on an annual term. It combines detection engineering, round-the-clock monitoring, investigation and agreed containment action. Orvix delivers it on two tracks: an in-region track for workloads with data residency obligations, and a global track for workloads without them, chosen per workload rather than per customer.

Questions We Are Asked

What is the difference between MDR and a SOC?
A security operations center is an organizational function; managed detection and response is a service you buy. MDR provides the detection engineering, the 24/7 analyst coverage, the investigation, and an agreed level of containment action, without requiring you to staff and retain that capability yourself.
Can our data stay in-country?
Workloads with a residency obligation run on the in-region track, where telemetry, storage, and analyst access are constrained to the required jurisdiction. The classification is recorded per workload at onboarding, with the obligation that drives it, and reviewed when either changes. In markets where security operations require a license, the service runs through a licensed local partner under its own license, named in your contract.
Who is allowed to take action in our environment?
Only what you have agreed in writing. Containment authority is defined at onboarding as two lists: actions analysts may take without asking, and actions that always require your approval. There is no implicit authority and no standing administrative access beyond the agreed scope.
Who audits the service you provide?
An independent party, which is what makes the opinion worth having. Assurance over a service Orvix operates is written by a party that does not report to the delivery team, or by a fully independent third party when the opinion needs external weight. Delivery and assurance of the same function are always contracted separately.
How long does onboarding take?
Thirty to forty-five days for a typical environment. That covers telemetry design and connection, workload residency classification, detection engineering for your environment, containment authority agreement, and a tested escalation path before the service goes live.
